title: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF)
everyday_terms: fever and joint pain that comes and goes
summary: Familial Mediterranean fever causes repeated attacks of fever with pain in the tummy, chest or joints. Attacks usually last a few days, and people feel well in between.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the MEFV gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy. A small number of people with one changed copy have attacks, and a doctor can explain this.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies usually has FMF, although some have few or no attacks. It is managed with daily treatment from a specialist team, which also helps protect the kidneys.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has FMF. Could I be a carrier?
What does a test for the MEFV gene involve?
card_summary: Repeated attacks of fever and pain. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Repeated fever attacks; managed with daily treatment from a specialist.
care: Rheumatology clinics, kidney clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
counsellor_questions: Which carrier test is right for me?
If I'm a carrier, could my partner be tested too?
